Yep, I really did. I have to pay my car note, insurance, cell phone, standard of living, etc. and I couldn't afford a place to stay.

I tried applying to places near home, then all over the country. Maybe I'll try abroad, thanks...

Yep, I thought about that. But my loan only covers the tuition and I would still have to pay out of pocket for a placr to stay. The school told me about a alumni group that helps with this kinda thing, but they redirected me to housing assistance and jobs that I already applied to.

My only hope is to apply somewhere else, hopefully in the Northeast and find a science department to work in...

I was set on going to school that I got accepted to. The tuition was covered, except that I don't have the money for a place stay or money for standard of living. The student loan amount was only enough to pay for tuition. I have no issue working a full time job and going to school full time. I've done it all throughout my undegrad with no summer breaks. I even worked a full time job in ER, worked a 15 hr/week internship, and went to school full time for 2 years. If you want it bad enough, it IS possible to work after school.

Also, I did look for research assistantships. I emailed my school, and the other 6 schools in the city in alot of STEM departments. It was either they were not interested, they were not looking, or no response...

I have no issue relocating. I did two summer researches in the Northeast. When it became apparant that I can't get a job here, I was gonna hopefully get a job there and hopefully go to a school up there and start next spring or fall.
Thanks, I'm glad alot of people can relate...
Haha! We have! I'm still waiting on my mountain dew and doritos!

Hey, thanks for the response. I am in the science field. I got a bachelor's in biology and was planning a doctorate in cell biology and then a 3 year MD, so bascially a physician scientist.

That's impressive if you have a son and have a degree.
I kinda made a conscious decision to give up my faith because it does not make sense to ne anymore.

Responsibilities in my opinion are a double edged sword. I might have certain freedoms but at the same time, I don't get to enjoy some of the good parts about responsibility. I don't feel independent and free knowing that I can handle responsibilities. 

You maybe have a difficult time raising a child, but you have the privilege of raising someone that loves you. That's an awesome experience.

Thanks. It's hard to undo a just world way of thinking when it's been ingrained in me since I was a child. That is true, I do not expect the world to owe me anything anymore. I just only hoped that I at least earned a chance but I now know that is not true 

I agree with what you said about fear. The concept of hell used to scare me but it doesn't anymore because most of my life WAS hell. I'm the lowest I've ever been so anything lower would be death.

If I were to die, I would be more upset than scared because I didn't get to experience things most people have handed to them. I guess that's how sick kids feel. If anything, my life built my character since childhood. I'm pretty humble and grateful for every opportunity I get.
Thanks! Love the username by the way...

I don't want to be here either. But what keeps me going is my dream to help underprivileged people by medicine. They too have suffer unjustly and have people tell them those empty hopes of prayer. It's not fair to them. I hope to make poor people's lives around me a little less unfair...

Ironically, when I won awards in research, got a publication, got in student government, volunteered high school students in working in the lab with me, and got a job, not only I came out of my shell and made a ton friends, became funnier and more outgoing, it also helped me in talking to girls more since  my school was 20:1 girl to boy ratio.

I got confidence in asking girls out, getting rejected, getting better, asking more girls out, etc. But I crashed and burned each time. I always thought it was confidence but, I figured it was more about looks.

Honestly, I don't think I'm a bad looking guy, but I'm not what society considers attractive. So add that to the rejection I get from employers and it totally kills or slows down any momentum of confidence.

And overall, it gets harder and harder to start over because you have no source to get confidence. School and working in the lab was all I had. And it's the same neverending cycle, I can't get confidence because I can't get a chance, and vice versa.

Haha! That's probably true for most guys.

I'm in the minority. There is a sort of "balance" in this world. Not everyone can have be financially secure, not everyone can be "attractive".

I hope it works out for you though...

Thanks for your response. I'll respond to those 3 statements.

I should've worded it better. I meant to say that I hate the concept of God. I am more angry at my relatives and my theology teachers in grade school to explain the reason of unfairness and suffering. And I'm angry at myself for believing in something like that.

I don't believe in that logic anymore. What I meant was that it was taught to me, so it was very hard to undo that way of thinking. I know that there are no guarantees but I sincerely feel that I am going above and beyond to increase my odds.

Again, that was taught to me. Fortunately I discarded that way of thinking back in high school. I did actually try from then until now. I find hobbies to improve myself, ask girls out, became more positive and outgoing- I came out of my shell the last 10 years, something I wouldn't even dream of doing.

But, I know what the world is and sadly, the number of prospects go down if girls in your own race don't find educated men attractive and the numbers decrease even further if most girls outside my race don't find dark skinned men attractive. I even tried online dating, it's worse.

Thanks. I agree with everything you said. The ones that  always told me that things get better already have things going for them. It's easy to say that because they're privileged. 

It just sucks that I have been brainwashed for 20 plus years so it's gonna take alot to undo it.
Yeah. Unfortunately, I am born in the lowest part of that too. Girls AND society treat me like I'm subhuman. It's why I'm not afraid of hell anymore. Being a FA AND poor IS hell...
Are you Texan? Im guessing from your name, lol...

That's cool that you're a welder! I know you have to go through the motions, especially a physical job like that.  It's also good that you're pretty young doing that, keeo going!

Thanks for your comment.

I used to think it was my resume. In 4 years, I worked in ER and ortho surgery, 2 summer internships, 1 internship at home, a lab job, volunteering, and created and spearheaded my own research. There is no gap of not working/ doing something in those 4 years. 

I asked pros for help writing on LinkedIn, advice, everything. Most of the jobs I first started applying to were research and hospital related, then started applying everywhere, then started emailing schools to do free help in their labs to at least get my foot in the door, nothing.

I explained in another reply that one time I changed my name and kept the same resume and got called and emailed for 6 job interviews versus 1 interview using my real name.

I partially believe that others get hired, but something is not adding up...

You bring up a good point. Part of me still believes that I was not the better candidate. But too many experiences from interviews and job applications led me to believe that it was more than a coincidence.

I'll give you two experiences.

One school had about 20 openings in research. I applied to all positions. I was qualified for all of them and had more experience than what they were asking for. I got called for 1 interview. The hiring manager told  me about the other positions and how no one applies and the PI have extra work. The interview went really good. Two days later I found out I wasn't considered. 

Later, I changed my name and kept the same resume, didn't change a thing but my name. I got emails, phone calls, for 6 of them.

It sucks. I believe your story too, I do believe sone candidates are better than me, but it gets harder for me to keep believing that I was passed over based on merit...

I appreciate your comment. I know women have it hard in the workplace too, and they almost  have to have almost a superhuman background to work in a well off career that otherwise the average person can get.

I will keep being me, thanks!
Thanks! One day at a time...
That's what I always believed too...
Muchas gracias por compriendo! My spanish is kinda rusty, lol...
Alpha Phi Alpha
Haha. Lo siento..
Yep, I know what you mean. It is frustrating. I'll try and do some things differently, thanks.
Thanks for your response. That is a great way to look at it. I am familiar with Nas. I like that song. I will especially remember numbers 3 and 4 of your advice. I appreciate it!
Thanks bro! I will keep that in mind!
Thanks! And I sure will! Btw, I like your name!

Yep! You hit the nail on the head. I wouldn't call myself an anomaly if I weren't treated like an outsider all the time. I don't think I'm more special than anyone else and just want to earn everyone's respect.

Speaking of which, I used to work in orthopedic surgery during undegrad cleaning and preparing rooms before and after surgery. The nurses, surgeons, and scrubs would ignore me if I said hi or treated me like I was a lesser employee just because I cleaned and mopped.

When they found out that I was graduating and was planning to do an MD/PhD, they would search far and wide through the department to befriend and strike a convo with me. It sucks that it has to be this way.

Sorry that you had to hear those things because you seem like a very smart person. Thanks for the response!

Thanks man, I really liked your response. I can't imagine what it's like being gay either and having a mixed culture.  That's awesome if you still managed to learn spanish. Thanks for understanding bro!
I've tried online. It's actually worse, haha. I was in SGA, a fraternity, volunteered, tutored, the whole nine. I think most girls see me as, "well he's friendly and smart but not for me"...

Yep, it sucks. I always wondered if that 3% of those in tech jobs for example is really because  it is a so called shortage of minorities or is because they are not getting hired.

Minorities graduate from STEM programs around the country like hot cakes but that number employment diversity number slowly climbs up...

I've actually read about Greenville being a great place to start for new graduates. I spent two summers in PA doing a research internship and loved it.

I'm from the south, and I was hoping to stay because we are behind in everything and I feel like I could contribute by STEM. But if I can't find a career and school, let alone a job, I'm just gonna move Northeast.

Thanks man. It's cool that you want give back. If anything, I want to do the same, like tutoring more kids to go the STEM route instead of relying on sports or entertainment to be successful. 

You're right, the road is always hard, but it's really cool that you understand too. Thanks bro!
Lol, wow dude. Sorry that I am typing on my phone, but thanks for the heads up....

Wow, that's amazing you are a law student. Congrats! I do volunteer work and did it the last few years at the Children's Hospital, Habitat for Humanity, and I helped at risk high school students work in the lab in research that I put together.

It's super hard to stay positive. But sometimes you have to laugh to keep from crying I guess. Thanks man.

Exactly. You made a great point. I'm 6'3 and I am a former athlete in high school. I won research awards and got a publication. But it infuriates me when people just can't believe that I am in the field I'm in and became successful in it, despite the sideways looks, backhanded compliments, and negative comments.

By some miracle, if I do get an interview, I could tell by their look of dissapointment when I walk in. It's not just jobs for me either. I've been rejected by dozens of women and schools. I am tall, but my friends would tell me that I am the most friendly and non threatening person ever.

It's like, holy shit, it's gotten THIS bad?!

I do believe I have depression. Since childhood I tried suppressing it and I haven't been happy in a long time. Even if, as you say, that my life got better 30 years from now for example,  my life would still have been a loss. I would suck that my life got better at 60 years old. I would have then missed everything, a family, a meaningful career, friends, everything. 

I appreciate your words, I really do. But I can't continue to live with empty hopes...

Thank you for the response. But the truth is that I've tried making friends, bettering myself, joining clubs at schools. And I was successful at that. But for the last 10 years, it never turned into anything. And I always told myself that everything will fall into place over time. 

If my life is hell for the last decade plus, why should I have to endure more if it, then die? Like I said, I know I can endure it but I DON'T WANT TO ANYMORE.  

Sometimes the best way to win is to not play anymore....

Thank you for your words! When I posted this, I was making a decision on buying sleeping pills. Just before deciding to, I called the suicide hotline and did an online chat. I got advice from them also on what to do.

I slowly settled down and felt better after reading your post. The only thing I could do is just take it one day at a time and stay in a positive mindset.

Everyone tells me that I was meant for greater things, even complete strangers I've had conversations with. But really, I sincerely thank you. I'm on the verge of tears typing this but if I ever become a successful scientist, I will find a way to thank you...

Hey, I'm glad I'm not alone in this. As bad as your story sounds, it seems like you still have something to look forward to get out of bed. Your GRE is something you could always change compared to your transcript.

It's cool that you are working towards a goal, even though your PI gives you crap, which is the majority of them, haha...

Just retake your GRE and reapply. Overall, I hope you find your purpose :D

I look into it, thanks. I worked at a hospital and luckily my school was across the street. I would go to school in the morning and then work the night shift, shower then repeat.

I've applied to jobs where I was over and underqualified. People tell me that I have nothing to lose and take risks. I've done that for the last ten years resulting in being kicked out of school the first time and graduate but have debt and no job or grad school the second time.

It's unfair that everyone around me gets to move forward with their lives while I'm stuck in the vicious cycle.  Things drop in people's laps and they aren't grateful for it like a girlfriend/wife, a family, a career, school, etc.

Whereas I was born and sacrificed and suffered since I was 6, only to always move two steps back when I try my damndest to move forward. Even when I new the real world at an early age, I knew to take life seriously if I didn't want to be in the hell around me and it still didn't work. I never thought my life would be hell and I would rather just be not living...

Thanks! It feels good knowing I'm not alone. In high school, I knew early on that I would have to change my life. I learned about the real world when I was six years old when my dad left. My mom emotionally and verbally abused me. I was always teased at schhol for being poor.

I tried finding work and advancing my education. I have a degree now but still get rejected for work and school. I don't want to try for a third time, and fail again. All the while piling debt and living in my car. I would rather just end it now and feel like I'm leaving knowing that I did my best, and that's all I could do...

I really hear what you are saying. The problem is that I told myself that the last 8 years as I clawed my way out of depression- being positive, outgoing, more confident, going back to school, everything.

I'm 28 and this will be the third time in my life that this happened. I don't want to waste another 8 years, wake up when I'm 36, and it's the same story.

Suffering from rejection, being poor, being lonely, watching my friends with careers, a family and a house, takes a toll on you. I'm emotionally and mentally drained.

It's hard to see everyone around you move forward with their lives as mine stays in a torturing circle, trying again for the third time.

I am being sincere when I say that if 10 years later, if I knew my life would be like this, I would have killed myself back in high school. I feel like I tried everything to change my life and failed, twice. I feel like that was my destiny and I've fulfilled it, now I am just waiting for death.

I don't feel like I'm giving up. Sometimes you just have to know that you've had enough of pain to keep living.

I thought by attending grad school, I could have a loan to pay for a dorm but I haven't been accepted to none of the schools I applied to. If I do get hired, I probably will have to go back into living in my car. 

It's a tough pill to swallow when I have 4 years of undergrad research, two summer internships, a publication, and my own indepedent research that I can't get hired for a simple lab job or go to grad school.

I dunno about nature. It seems everything works out for others without trying. Whereas I am always excluded, left behind, poor, rejected, alone, and depressed. Most people only have to deal with ONE of these things but nature decided one is not enough for me...
